both blocks' complete P0 proofs, each with its own 135 claim values, 12 sumchecks, 4 collapses and 3 non-hiding openings

public_residual_seam_as_shipped.mechanism: block 0's expected OUTPUT tensor and block 1's expected INPUT tensor are the SAME 512 public INT16 words; each block binds its own end of it with bind_endpoints, so the residual is carried by a PUBLIC tensor, not by an MLE equality between two commitments
public_residual_seam_as_shipped.source: public_chain_receipt.rs:127-148 block_expectations; public_block_receipt.rs:255-284 bind_endpoints; FA5 R26/R27
what_a_private_profile_must_change: the intermediate tensor cannot be published: the residual becomes an MLE equality between block k's attention A and block k+1's attention A, i.e. layer_seam's relation under a masked-equality gadget (private_seam.rs's form) with its own CFS slot and reserved pair rows
block k's attention A may not finalize before block k+1 has bound the residual seam (FA3 section 4.5), so a chain holds two AttnPending objects; nothing in attention.rs enforces that ordering today
bind_endpoints' external I/O binding stays public only for the declared boundary; every intermediate binding must move inside

All 19 share one opening group (col_key None, all-ones column weights). The FFN has exactly ONE such claim and masks it with a zero_sum_pair plus a fresh pair h_up (FA2 14.5). Nineteen independent sums over five different domains have no analogue in FA2/FA3 and no inventory row anywhere.

Each limb is its own claim, so each needs its own mask row: a single shared mask would leave limb DIFFERENCES in the clear (zk.rs:1974-1977's rationale). Latent at this profile (Cls::Int16 -> 1 limb); it bites under Cls::Int24 (2 limbs).
FA3 2.3 item 6: a flipped-point claim is a separate group with its own reserved pair. Each is a SINGLETON group here.
Not a mask site: the histograms are published in full. A private profile needs the FFN's committed-table construction; the single-row table slots below are FA2 U10's pair-needed case.
